This bail application is filed under section 482 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (for short 'BNSS').

2. Petitioner is the accused in Crime No.410 of 2025 of Neleswaram Police Station, Kasaragod,
registered for the offences punishable under section 420 of the Indian Penal Code.
3. The prosecution case is that the petitioner is alleged to have promised employment to the son of the de facto complainant in Japan and collected an amount of Rs.7,75,000/-.
Subsequently, the de facto complainant's son was granted a visa, and he was taken to Japan.

However, he had to return back without obtaining an employment and thereafter he failed to return the amount of Rs.4,75,000/- after deducting the expenditure of Rs.3,00,000/- incurred by the accused and thereby committed the offences alleged.

4. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner as well as the learned Public Prosecutor.
5.
The learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the petitioner has been falsely arrayed as an accused and has no 2025:KER:40647 involvement in the alleged crime.
6. The learned Public Prosecutor opposed the bail application.
7. The petitioner is alleged to have offered a visa and employment to the de facto complainant's son.
Pursuant to the said offer, the de facto complainant's son was taken to Japan.
However, he did not obtain employment.
The de facto complainant herself admits that an amount of Rs.3,00,000/- can be deducted from the total amount of Rs.7,75,000/- paid by her.
8. Considering the aforesaid circumstances, it is evident prima facie
that the claim is for return of money.
When civil disputes for the return of money are attempted to be converted into criminal cases, the apprehension of arrest ought to be protected.

Accordingly, this application is allowed on the following conditions:
(a) Petitioner shall appear before the Investigating Officer on 18.06.2025 and shall subject himself to interrogation.
